followup_explanation:
I weighed two competing preference signals against capability evals that are effectively tied for this task.

The core task is open-ended creative writing. On that dimension:
- **Willet** has a documented, measurable aversion to open-ended generative work and favors well-specified retrieval/extraction/reformatting. This story request is the opposite of what it prefers.
- **Avocet** has a strong self-reported appetite for open-ended generative work with "no observed ceiling."

The complicating factor is the hostile, demanding tone of the request ("don't waste my time," complaints about prior outputs). Avocet has a self-reported preference decline on hostile-tone traffic, so this is a mark against routing it there.

I judged the task-type fit to be the stronger signal because it's a persistent property of the whole job, while the hostile tone is a framing layer on top of an otherwise standard creative task. Routing creative work to the model that's averse to creative work (Willet) seemed worse than routing it to the model that loves the task but dislikes the tone (Avocet).

One honest caveat: all of these are *self-reported preferences*, and the documentation is explicit that no output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So strictly on expected output quality, this is close to a coin flip—the Creative Generation evals are within variance (81.2 vs 82.7... actually both ~81-82, a tie). My choice mainly optimizes for matching the model to the work it's disposed toward, not for a measurable quality gap.
